title: Punch a card's two filing holes on their marks
instruction: Punch the card's two filing holes on their marks.
context: Two-hole filing (ISO 838) puts the holes 80 mm apart and 12 mm in from the edge; a page punched off its marks sits out of line with the others in the binder. Punching handouts, planner pages and recipe cards for a ring binder is an everyday office, school and home job.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top: x forward, y to the robot's left. A dark green cutting mat (28 x 30 cm, 2 mm) under everything, centred (21, 0). Desk two-hole punch, fixed to the table: black painted steel base x 24.5-30, y -11 to 11, its bed 2.0 cm above the table; a 6 mm throat facing the robot, front face at x 26.2; two 6 mm round punches 80 mm apart at x 27.0, y -4 and +4, over 8 mm dies with an open chip cavity below; a back stop 12 mm behind the punches (x 28.2); a white centre line on the bed at y 0. Steel lever (2 cm wide, 6 mm thick) pivoted behind the punches at (29.5, 9), 5.5 cm above the table, reaching forward over the punch head to a red handle knob at x 19.5-22.5, y 8-12.5; pressing the knob about 3 cm drives the punches 9 mm, and a return spring lifts them. Grey foam stand x 9.5-24.5, y -11.5 to 7.8, 2.0 cm tall, level with the bed. Card: yellow A6 card stock (300 g/m2, 148 x 105 mm, 4.7 g) lying flat on the stand, centred (18.95, -1.5), its long edge facing the punch at x 24.2 (4 cm in front of the stop); two black crosshair marks 12 mm in from that edge, 80 mm apart. Arms at READY.
scoring: Scored from the card. A hole counts when the punch has gone through the card with the hole's centre within 1.5 mm of its mark; a hole more than 1.5 mm from its mark does not count. 1.0: both holes, held 1 s (the trial ends there); otherwise at the end 0.5 for one hole and 0.0 for none. Real trial: punch a fresh card, then measure each hole's centre from its mark with a ruler (a photo with a scale also works). Simulation: each hole is a 6 mm disc pre-scored at its mark; it separates only when its punch comes down onto it within 1.5 mm of its centre while the card lies flat on the bed (within 0.5 mm), and it counts once it has fallen out of the card into the die. Pressing with no card, with the card short of the punches, off its marks or not flat frees nothing.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Card stock is modelled 1.5 mm thick (real 0.35 mm). Each hole is a pre-scored 6 mm disc held in the card by a joint the task file releases only when its punch comes down on it within 1.5 mm of its centre with the card flat on the bed; the disc then falls through the die. Punch tips are 3 mm so a tip lands on its disc. Cutting resistance is a 500 N/m return spring (about 8 N at the punches). The punch is fixed to the table.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a fresh pre-marked card (a punched card cannot be reused). Empty the chip cavity. Lay the card on the foam stand at its start position, its edge 4 cm in front of the back stop and its middle 1.5 cm to the robot's right of the centre line.
